clue.text: Measuring tool for working vehicle

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
a tractor is a farm vehicle built for work

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a gauge suited to a working vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometry instrument for measuring angles, a semicircle marked in degrees.

clue.text: Cut up old jersey?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: An old sweater has been cut into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LOP into POL, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo shirt or polo neck is a kind of knitted top, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: What's surgeon doing lecturing about exercises?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: orating is giving a formal speech
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a surgeon is giving a talk about workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon at work in theatre is carrying out an operation.

clue.text: Delivery-maker's preparation

parts.note: a cricket bowler, who makes deliveries, sprints in before releasing the ball; also the build-up before any event

explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery-maker' suggests a courier or midwife; in cricket the bowler delivers the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the bowler's approach to the crease before bowling has this name.

clue.text: Caught a lad or criminal — that's what you get in an estate, say

definitions.text: that's what you get in an estate, say

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A young offender is arrested, the kind of thing that happens on a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' means an estate car (a station wagon), not a housing estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A full vehicle's worth of goods or people is what fits in an estate car, an example of a car.

clue.text: The place for fruit or toast: beginning of day

parts.note: to char is to scorch or toast

indicators.note: beginning of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A breakfast choice between fruit and toast at the start of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees are grown together in this kind of planted enclosure.

clue.text: Weapons since held by Royal Marines? On the contrary

indicators.note: held by places one piece inside another, and 'On the contrary' swaps which holds which
this reverses the stated relationship, so the second piece holds the first

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.surface: A question about weapons carried by British commandos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' tells you to swap the container and contents that 'held by' would otherwise imply.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns and other armaments are collectively called by this word.

clue.text: Egyptian god one thanks for food

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
I is the Roman numeral one
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone thanks an Egyptian deity for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian yoghurt side dish with cucumber, a specific kind of food.

clue.text: Piece of advice from guests: go in drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tip addressed to party guests urging them to enter tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A recommendation offered to someone is a proposal or hint of what to do.

clue.text: Keep one's head down — Eastender's fibbing, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the result is a sound-alike of the spoken words

parts.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops the final g, saying lyin' for lying

explanation.surface: Advice to stay low because a Londoner is telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eastender is a Cockney from east London, whose speech drops final g's.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed late in the morning keeps your head on the pillow.

clue.text: Tape head in rage and end corgi's barking

indicators.note: head in picks the first letter of the following word
barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy into a new order

parts.note: corgi with the 's as a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A clip of a corgi barking furiously at the end of its tether.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape is a recorded piece of audio or video, a stored track.

clue.text: Soldier even fixed uniform

definitions.meaning: a professional full-time soldier in a standing army
even as in steady and unvarying
fixed as in a set, scheduled routine
uniform as in consistent, the same throughout

explanation.surface: A soldier even repaired a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a professional army man and steadiness, being set, and being consistent.

clue.text: A parliamentarian almost had to purchase gold jar

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: a purchase is a grip or hold, so one piece grips the other
almost removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An MP nearly had to buy a golden vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying but means a grip: HA holds OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek two-handled vessel for wine or oil, a type of jar.

clue.text: Serious French accent?

definitions.meaning: the backward-sloping mark over a letter, as on è, used in French

explanation.walkthrough: 'French accent' suggests a way of speaking, but it is a written diacritic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means solemn, and also names the diacritical mark seen in French spelling.

clue.text: Thought that's returned when at one's dressing-table?

definitions.text: that's returned when at one's dressing-table?
definitions.meaning: the image a mirror sends back

explanation.definitionFit: The word means contemplation and also the image a mirror throws back.

clue.text: Was present small and left outside?

indicators.note: outside puts one word around the other

parts.note: exited means went out, left

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone attended, briefly, before going outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is a verb, departed, not the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been present is to have had being, a near synonym for having lived.

clue.text: Blood-sucking mite was first to get excited

parts.note: a tick is a small bloodsucking arachnid
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: A parasite was the first creature to become agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickled means amused or thrilled, delighted and excited.

clue.text: Charm of French entertaining

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
light as in light entertainment, easy and amusing

explanation.surface: The allure of French hospitality.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to please and enchant them.

clue.text: Agree aunt's broken promise

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: aunt with the 's read as is, a link

explanation.surface: Someone agrees their aunt went back on her word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge or assurance given to someone is a firm undertaking.

clue.text: Sound from record and I almost cry

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: almost removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: a call is a cry

explanation.surface: Hearing a recording, someone nearly bursts into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is an adjective, as in sound reasoning, not noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reasoning is rational and coherent.

clue.text: Suitcases seen as joke in toboggan

indicators.note: in places the joke inside the sled

parts.note: a luge is a small racing toboggan
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Bags used as a prank on a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags and cases taken on a journey are a traveller's baggage.

clue.text: Wind pulled a daughter over

parts.note: a muscle pulled is a muscle torn
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A gust dragged a girl off her feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm, a twister, is one kind of wind.

clue.text: Time given to composer's passages

parts.note: Ravel was a French composer; with 's

explanation.surface: A conductor allots time to passages by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passages' suggests musical passages, but means journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Passages as in voyages or journeys; one's travels are one's trips abroad.

clue.text: Animal arrived then left

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: A creature turned up and then went away.
explanation.definitionFit: A humped desert beast is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Acts out being married with property, upwardly mobile

indicators.note: in a down clue, upwardly mobile means the word moves up, reading backwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British property

explanation.surface: A newly-wed social climber with a house is putting on a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, two homes sharing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing silently with gestures only is miming, acting something out.

clue.text: First-class degree for relative

parts.note: grand means splendid, first-rate
an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A top-grade qualification earned for a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandparent, a parent's mother, is a family relative.

clue.text: Play dead, oddly, when animal enters

indicators.note: enters puts the animal inside the other letters
oddly picks the first, third and following odd-numbered letters

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An instruction to play dead whenever a beast approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes D and A from 'dead'; RAM goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece of theatre, a work of stage drama.

clue.text: Flower one gentleman picked up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the word is lifted to read backwards

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man picks a single bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall purple or yellow garden plant with sword-shaped leaves is one kind of flower.

clue.text: Sudden energy after I am timed swimming

indicators.note: after places the energy letter at the end
swimming suggests the letters float about into a new arrangement

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A swimmer gets a burst of energy once the stopwatch starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something instant and without delay happens suddenly.

clue.text: Part female's wanting, one in a film maybe

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a factor is a contributing part or element
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman lacks a role, as might someone hoping to appear in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' suggests a role in a film, but means FACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer playing a role on screen is an example of someone appearing in a film.

clue.text: Starts to notice old Scotch egg — it smells

indicators.note: starts picks the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Someone first notices an old Scotch egg is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scotch egg is a British snack: a boiled egg in sausage meat and breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of scent on the face is what does the smelling.

clue.text: Novel's hard to leave perhaps — reviewed in the press?

parts.note: novel means new, with the 's giving S

indicators.note: reviewed means looked at again, so the letters are rearranged
to leave means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A novel is hard to put down, perhaps, according to reviews in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H from PERHAPS gives PERAPS, which 'reviewed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is the collective name for printed journalism, the daily papers.
